analysis: The withheld-item MultVAE–SASRec ensemble achieved measured macro validation HR@10 of 0.6225, below the supplied 0.6250 baseline by 0.0025. Per-category HR@10 was 0.695 for Movies_and_TV, 0.650 for Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.455 for Electronics, and 0.690 for CDs_and_Vinyl. Execution succeeded, but this trial does not support replacing the baseline with withheld-item supervision. Aggregate results alone cannot establish whether masking reduced the suspected residual identity shortcut. The trial consumed 923.025 allocated GPU-seconds.
code_summary: Retains four independently trained category ensembles. MultVAE uses a 256-dimensional encoder, 64-dimensional variational latent, full-catalog multinomial reconstruction, annealed KL, and an encoder-to-decoder residual connection. During training, half of each deduplicated history is withheld as reconstruction targets; both encoder and residual receive only retained context, normalized by inverse square-root context length. Singletons reconstruct themselves. SASRec retains shared item embeddings and one-negative BCE. Independently selected expert checkpoints are combined using equal-weight, average-tie normalized rank fusion. Exported prediction restores checkpoint configurations and uses complete histories without masking. Existing reload and predictor parity checks remain; dedicated masking and gradient checks were not added. Budget accounting and printed baseline comparisons still contain stale values.
